issues.legal_issue: The Supreme Court may set aside concurrent factual findings in a special-leave appeal when they are manifestly unjust and cause grave injustice.
material_facts: The appeal was brought by special leave after the trial court, the lower appellate court, and the High Court had all rejected the claim.

The lower courts' finding on readiness and willingness rested on an adverse inference from the absence of a bank passbook even though no one had asked for it to be produced, and overlooked evidence concerning the defendant's failure to attend the Sub-Registrar's office.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court could re-examine and set aside the concurrent findings because they were manifestly unreasonable and perpetuated grave injustice.
issues.legal_principle: Article 136 of the Constitution gives the Supreme Court discretionary special-leave jurisdiction and does not require it to leave manifest injustice uncorrected merely because findings are concurrent. The Court relied on Variety Emporium v. Mohd. Ibrahim Naina, which states that once the burden of showing a concurrent decision is manifestly unjust is discharged, the Court has a duty to remedy the injustice.

rule.if: special_leave_appeal and concurrent_findings and finding_manifestly_unjust and grave_injustice

predicates.special_leave_appeal: A party brings an appeal to the Supreme Court by special leave.
predicates.concurrent_findings: Two or more lower courts reach the same finding on an issue.
predicates.finding_manifestly_unjust: The concurrent finding is manifestly unreasonable in light of the evidence and applicable law.
predicates.grave_injustice: Leaving the finding undisturbed would perpetuate grave injustice.

issues.definition: When a special-leave appeal challenges concurrent findings that are manifestly unjust and would perpetuate grave injustice, those findings may be set aside.

issues.legal_issue: A stipulated deadline does not make time essential to a contract for sale of immovable property when the contract and the parties' case do not establish that intention.
material_facts: The agreement required the property to be conveyed within ten years.
The defendant did not plead or testify that time was essential, and the agreement did not unmistakably express that intention.
The lower courts nevertheless treated time as essential.
issues.conclusion: The lower courts erred in treating time as essential to the contract.
issues.legal_principle: The normal presumption for an agreement to sell immovable property is that time is not of the essence; the parties' intention must be assessed from the contract and the circumstances. The Court relied on Govind Prasad Chaturvedi v. Hari Dutt Shastri, which also cautions against deciding that time is essential when the issue was not pleaded or tried.

predicates.immovable_property_sale_agreement: The parties made an agreement for the sale of immovable property.
predicates.no_unmistakable_time_essential_term: The agreement does not unmistakably state that timely performance is essential to the bargain.
predicates.no_party_asserted_time_essential: No party pleaded or advanced the case that time was essential to the contract.

issues.definition: For an agreement to sell immovable property, where the agreement does not unmistakably make time essential and no party asserts that it is, time is not essential.

issues.legal_issue: A purchaser who takes the steps reasonably available to perform an agreement may establish readiness and willingness where the vendor, despite notice, fails to attend for completion; an adverse inference from missing documents is not justified when their production was never sought.
material_facts: The purchaser said he had arranged the purchase money, including by borrowing, and had deposited money in a bank.
Neither the defendant nor the court asked the purchaser to produce his passbook before the lower courts drew an adverse inference from its absence.
Before the contractual deadline, the purchaser sent the defendant a registered notice and a telegram asking him to attend the Sub-Registrar's office.
The purchaser attended the office on the appointed day and obtained a record of his attendance.
The defendant's accounts of receiving notice and attending the office were inconsistent, and the Court concluded that he had not attended and was not willing to perform.
The purchaser sought specific performance of the agreement.
issues.conclusion: The purchaser was ready and willing to perform, the defendant had breached the agreement, and the purchaser was entitled to specific performance.
issues.legal_principle: Readiness and willingness must be assessed from the evidence as a whole, including the other party's willingness and conduct; a purchaser is not required to do more when he has given notice and attended for completion but the vendor does not attend. Under Mst. Ramrati Kuer v. Dwarika Prasad Singh, an adverse inference from a party's failure to produce material documents is not justified where their production was not requested and the party did not then fail to comply with an order to produce them.

rule.if: specific_performance_suit and purchaser_gave_completion_notice and purchaser_attended_for_completion and vendor_failed_to_attend and no_request_to_produce_missing_document

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The purchaser brings a suit seeking specific performance of an agreement to sell property.
predicates.purchaser_gave_completion_notice: The purchaser notified the vendor in time that the purchaser would attend to complete the transaction.
predicates.purchaser_attended_for_completion: The purchaser attended at the agreed place to complete the transaction.
predicates.vendor_failed_to_attend: The vendor did not attend to perform the vendor's part of the agreement.
predicates.no_request_to_produce_missing_document: No party or court asked the purchaser to produce the missing document before drawing an adverse inference from its absence.

issues.definition: In a specific-performance suit, where the purchaser gives timely notice and attends for completion, the vendor fails to attend, and production of the missing document was never requested, specific performance is granted.
